'''Emilia Teresa Julia Currás Puente''' (8 October 1927 – 29 March 2020) was a Spanish [[information scientist]] and academic. She was also a philosopher and historian of science, as well as a pioneer in the study of the philosophical-scientific bases of Information and documentation.

==Biography and career==
She was born in [[Madrid]] on 8 October 1927 from [[Galician people|Galician]] parents<ref name="ISKO2021">{{Cite web|url=https://www.isko2021.letras.ulisboa.pt/emilia-curras/|title=ISKO 2021 LISBOA. Emilia Currás|website=[[University of Lisbon]]|language=es}}</ref> Currás and her family lived through the [[Spanish Civil War]] in [[Alberic, Valencia]]. After the war, the family moved to [[Tetuan]] where her mother worked as a teacher. In the middle of the 1940s, they returned to Madrid and Emilia Currás studied at the [[IES Lope de Vega|Lope de Vega]] secondary school.<ref name="LOdZEC">{{Cite journal|url=https://www.laopiniondezamora.es/blogs/sociedad/hablamos-de-mujeres/2014/11/08/emilia-curras-puente-1000476.html|journal={{ill|La Opinión-El Correo de Zamora|es}}|title=Hablamos de mujeres. Emilia Currás Puente.|first=Hortensia|last=Hernández|date=8 November 2014 |language=es}}</ref> She graduated from Chemical Sciences at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]] and the [[University of Santiago de Compostela]] in 1953.<ref name=LOdZEC /> She worked at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine as a research fellow in the Chair of Chemistry and at the [[Spanish National Research Council]] until 1955, when she entered [[Technische Universität Berlin]] to pursue doctoral studies, being invested as such in 1959.<ref name=LOdZEC />

She joined a private company in 1960, founding the Chemistry and Technical Translation Section of Hanumag-Barreiros (Madrid),<ref name= ISKO2021 /> moving a year later to the company Auxini-Piritas Españolas as head of the Documentation Department until 1964. She returned to Germany to become head of the Materials Analysis Laboratory of Linde AG (Köln-Suhn) in 1965, where she also enrolled at the Institute of Documentation in Frankfurt/Main, obtaining the title of Scientific Documentalist in 1966.<ref name=LOdZEC />

She continued in Germany until 1968 as head of the patent documentation section at Dynamit Nobel (Troisdorf). In 1969 she returned to Spain to found and direct the Documentation Department at Hispanoil (Madrid).<ref name="DiarioPublicoEmilia">{{Cite journal|url=https://blogs.publico.es/otrasmiradas/44841/el-legado-de-emilia-curras-quimica-poesia-y-la-ciencia-de-ordenar-el-conocimiento/|journal=[[Público (Spain)|Público]]|title=El legado de Emilia Currás: química, poesía y la ciencia de ordenar el conocimiento|first=Rosa|last=San Segundo|date=3 February 2021|language=es}}</ref>

In 1970 she left the private industry sector to join the Faculty of Sciences of the Autonomous University of Madrid and to direct the Scientific Documentation Office within the Department of Applied Chemistry-Physics.<ref name=DiarioPublicoEmilia />

On 3 May 1988 she was named a member of the {{ill|Spain's Royal Academy of Doctors|es|Real Academia de Doctores de España}}.<ref name="RADEEmCu">{{cite web|url=https://www.radoctores.es/academico.php?item=129|title=Emilia Currás Puente|website={{ill|Real Academia de Doctores de España|es}}|language=es|access-date=13 May 2021|archive-date=13 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513215919/https://www.radoctores.es/academico.php?item=129|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Fields of work==
===Philosophy and history of science===
Her most notable contribution is the creation of the Theory of Informationism and the Vertical Integration of Science, which appeared in 1981 and was accepted in 1988.<ref name= ISKO2021 /> Informationism was a new epistemology based on the neural theory of Information, or neural networks, where information reaches our brain in the form of tiny impulses called quanta of information that impact our neurons, activating them and converting these quanta into useful information.<ref name="CoreUKEmiliaC">{{Cite conference|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/11877643.pdf|title=INFORMACIONISMO Y ASIMILACIÓN NEURONAL DE LA INFORMACIÓN.|conference=I Congreso Internacional sobre Tecnología Documental y del Conocimiento|via=[[CORE (research service)|CORE]]|year=2003|language=es}}</ref>

According to Currás, this theory considers information as the axis of our life and as the motor of all neuronal and physical evolution of the human being; that is, the more useful information our brain receives, the greater our neuronal tissue will be, creating the beginning of the path of development of civilization and culture of any people.

Informationism is based on the paradigm of the universality of information, which is independent in itself as a scientific discipline, but which is systemically and vertically related to the other sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.radoctores.es/doc/1V5N2-curras-integracionvertical.pdf|website=Real Academia de Doctores de España|title=Integración vertical de las ciencias. Una aproximación científica (Desde una visión Sistémica)|year=2001|language=es|access-date=13 May 2021|archive-date=7 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207124144/https://www.radoctores.es/doc/1V5N2-curras-integracionvertical.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Documentation===
In this field, she was a pioneer in Spain and in many Spanish-speaking countries. She introduced the concept of Documentation Sciences as a nucleus that housed the different disciplines related to the processes of information contained in a document so that it can reach the user quickly, unequivocally and efficiently.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://issuu.com/legueinleguein/docs/revistaleguein2011|journal=Leguein Leguein Via Issuu|title=Una científica muy romántica|first1=Cristina|last1=Pascual|first2=Pilar|last2=del Campo|language=es|year=2011|archive-date=24 December 2023|access-date=13 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231224091602/https://issuu.com/legueinleguein/docs/revistaleguein2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> She worked on the design and construction of a [[Thesaurus (information retrieval)|thesaurus]], contributing with the creation of three manuals, where the thesaurus was approached from different perspectives: documentary linguistics, systems theory, ontology, taxonomy, information theory, computer science, etc.

In 1976 she founded the Spanish Society for Scientific Information and Documentation (SEDIC) in 1976, and was its president for twelve years.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://issuu.com/fundacioncd/docs/revista_documentacion3|journal=Revista Documentación via Issuu|title=Entrevista a Emilia Currás|first=M. Auxiliadora|last=Martín|date=31 December 2007|language=es|archive-date=29 September 2023|access-date=13 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230929075346/https://issuu.com/fundacioncd/docs/revista_documentacion3|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was a founding member of Hispano Term and ASEABI. She was also a member of the Council of the International Federation for Documentation (FID) for eight years.<ref name= RADEEmCu />

She was a member of the advisory and editorial boards of several journals such as the Journal of Information Science. She was also a member of organizations such as the [[American Library Association]] (ALA), the [[International Society for Knowledge Organization]] (ISKO) and the Prof. Kaula Foundation, among others.<ref name= RADEEmCu /><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://ruc.udc.es/dspace/handle/2183/11641|title=El devenir de ISKO-España hasta 1998. Actas del X Congreso de ISKO-España.|website=[[University of A Coruña]]|year=2013 |publisher=Universidade da Coruña |isbn=9788497495356 |language=es}}</ref>

===Chemistry===
She did research on molten antimony tribromide as an ionizing solvent (the subject of her thesis) resulting in the discovery of five new compounds, which were registered in the Index Chemicus database.<ref name=ISKO2021 /> She obtained an Excellent [[Cum Laude]] qualification. As a result of her research in this field, she was awarded the title of European Chemist by EURCHEN on several occasions.<ref name=LOdZEC /> She was a member of the Ilustre Colegio Oficial de Química (1993) and belonged to the Real Sociedad de Químicos de España (1988).<ref name=LOdZEC />

==Death==
Currás died on 29 March 2020 at the age of 92 in Madrid from [[COVID-19]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]].<ref name=DiarioPublicoEmilia />

==Publications==
She published more than 130 research articles in Spanish and foreign journals. She wrote 14 books and 7 as collective publications.<ref name="PrDeLaIn">{{Cite web|url=http://profesionaldelainformacion.com/contenidos/2009/julio/09.pdf|title=El documentalista en crisis|website=ThinkEpi via Profesional de la información|language=es}}</ref> Her work has been translated into English, Portuguese, Arabic and Czech,<ref name=PrDeLaIn /> and has received more than 200 citations.<ref name="WorldCatEMI">{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n84100602/|title=Currás, Emilia|website=[[WorldCat]]|language=en}}</ref>

Her publications include:<ref name=WorldCatEMI />
*''Information Science on Systemic and Systematic Postulates'' (2008).
*''Ontologies, Taxonomies, and Thesauri'' (2005)
*''Thesauri. Manual of construction and use'' (1998)
*''Treatise on Information Science'' (1996)
*''Thesauri. Terminological Languages'' (1991)
*''Information in its New Aspects: Documentation Sciences'' (1988)
*''Documentation Sciences: Library Science, Archival Science, Documentation and Information'' (1982).
*In 2003, ISKO published a tribute book entitled ''Una vida: profesión y pasión'' (A life: profession and passion).

Emilia Currás also wrote poetry, a passion she began at the age of 16, collected in three collections of poems: ''Fugitiva del tiempo'', ''Del pasar y corre amor'', ''En una tarde tibia''<ref name="IdealEmilia">{{Cite journal|url=https://www.elidealgallego.com/texto-diario/mostrar/2378972/voy-mirando-calle-alrededor-repente-viene-idea|journal=[[El Ideal Gallego]]|title="Voy mirando por la calle y a mi alrededor y de repente me viene una idea"|first=Marta|last=García Márquez|date=16 May 2013|language=es}}</ref> and ''El rincón de mis pensamientos''.

==Selected awards==
Among the numerous awards she received are:
*Gold Medal of the Prof. Kaula Foundation (1990).<ref name= RADEEmCu />
*Fellow of the Institute for Information Scientists, London (1992).<ref name= RADEEmCu />
*FEDINE Medal of Technological Merit (1997).<ref name= RADEEmCu />
*Honorary President of ISKO-Spain (1998).<ref name= RADEEmCu />
*Gold Badge of the [[:de:Deutsche Gesellschaft f%C3%BCr Information und Wissen|Deutsche Gesellschaft für Information und Wissen (DGI), the German Society of Information Specialists]] (2002).<ref name=LOdZEC />
*''Woman of the Year 2004'' of The [[American Biographical Institute]], being included in its yearbook ''Great women of the 21st Century''.<ref name=CoreUKEmiliaC /><ref name=LOdZEC />
*The [[King's College, Cambridge|King's College]] of [[Cambridge]] (UK) included her in the ''Outstanding Intellectuals of the 21st Century'' (2004).<ref name=LOdZEC />
*Honorary Member of the Hispanic Association of Internet Documentalists (AHDI) since 2004.<ref name=LOdZEC />
*Gold and Brilliant Badge of the Association of Chemists of Madrid (2011).<ref name=IdealEmilia />
*Numerary member of the International Brotherhood of Researchers of Toledo and honorary member of the SEDIC since 2013.
*Member of the [[Club of Rome]].<ref name= RADEEmCu />
*Knight's Cross awarded by the [[government of Colombia]].<ref name=IdealEmilia />
*She was decorated and honored by the universities of Düsseldorf, Zaragoza, Brasilia, San Marcos de Lima, Autónoma of Madrid, Opavá (Czech Republic), Complutense of Madrid and University of La Manouba (Tunisia).<ref name=IdealEmilia />
